newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL-Modelo Q2 seen strong on exports.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Modelo Q2 seen strong on exports.

text.p: Mexican brewer Grupo Modelo will show strong second quarter earnings underpinned by a surge in exports, analysts say.

A Reuters survey of four analysts forecast Modelo would post average net earnings of 437 million pesos for the second quarter of 1997, a nominal increase of 25.9 percent from the same period last year.
The analysts estimated net earnings per share for the second quarter at 0.54 peso, with individual forecasts ranging from 0.45-0.62 peso per share.
Modelo posted net earnings of 347 million pesos for the second quarter in 1996.

"On the whole I expect good numbers, especially due to the outlook for exports, " said Gregory Rianhard, an analyst with the Interacciones brokerage. Mexican beer exports in April, the most recent month for which figures are available, were up 66.6 percent compared with the same month last year, the National Statistics Institute (INEGI) announced.
Analysts said they saw beer exports for the second quarter up by 25-30 percent from the same quarter last year, above previous estimates of about 16 percent.
Analysts estimated Modelo had outpaced Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV, or Femsa, its sole Mexican competitor, in the exports race.
"I believe most growth in export volumes may be put down to Modelo. We estimate Femsa posted solid export volumes in April, but they were well below Modelo," Rianhard said.
Marco Vera, of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said "on this occasion, Modelo is doing better than Femsa."
Julio Zetina of Caspian Research said Modelo would also benefit from price hikes of 23 percent in March and growth in the domestic beer market.
Nonetheless, Jorge Gutierrez at the Inverlat brokerage predicted that recent price increases would eat into domestic sales volumes.
